Decided (Q1 = A and Q2 = A of the plan).** **Plane:** DEVDESK-303 (IS-12), dated 2026-11-13. Sources: `.claude/plans/DEVDESK-303-plan.md`, `docs/product/image-search/` (IS-12, IS-03, IS-13, IS-17), D129, D131, D132, `docs/architecture/network.md` ("Image search", "Level 1"), Rules 110, 128 and 139.
106:4. **H4: `dhi.io` is refused in `ByRegistry`, before routing.** `isDHI` matches the host exactly, case-insensitively, ignoring scheme, port and path. `registry.dhi.io` and `notdhi.io` are not matched. Neither searcher is called, which a counter test checks. Until IS-17 this is the only way dhi.io is searched, so its tags stay open.
108:6. **H6: the verdicts live in the browser for one lot.** `RegistryBrowser.outcomes` is reset by `startImageSearch`, read by `Outcome` and copied out by `RegistryBrowserOutcomes()`. Only `ok` appends rows. Nothing is shown: the header and the footer are unchanged, and IS-13 shows the verdicts (`+N`, `Failed`, `Refused`, `Pending`, `Partial`, `Skipped`).
109:7. **Deviation from the story, criterion 7 (accepted).** The `httptest` cases on `/v2/_catalog` (404/405 on the catalogue, the result cap, a prefix absent from the catalogue) need the catalogue walker, which is IS-03, planned after IS-12. Here, the cases are covered by the table of `Classify`, by the sentinels, and by `httptest` on the Hub endpoint (same `*oci.StatusError` path). The cap is tested end to end with a fake `Searcher` that returns `partial = true`. The `_catalog` tests move to IS-03 (criteria 3, 5, 7 and 8). To confirm in the PR.
110:8. **Risks handed to IS-13.** (a) A lot cut short by a new search or a closed browser leaves registries with no verdict; IS-13 must read a checked registry with no verdict and `pendingSearches == 0` as interrupted, not as pending. (b) Until IS-03, every private registry is `refused` in every search (D131); if IS-13 ships before IS-03, the header must not show `Refused: <each private registry>` on every search.
115:**D133 — DEVDESK-307 (IS-09): `←` or `esc` on tags opened with `→` returns to level 1 of the registry browser, untouched and with no new request; leaving the tags always cancels the tag lot. Decided (H1 to H5, validated by the user).** **Plane:** DEVDESK-307 (IS-09), dated 2026-11-13. Sources: `.claude/plans/DEVDESK-307-plan.md`, `docs/product/image-search/stories.md`, D129, D132, `docs/architecture/network.md` ("Back to level 1"), Rules 130 and 138.
125:**D132 — DEVDESK-304 (draft, to confirm): `→` at level 1 of the registry browser opens the usual tag table for the row under the cursor, on that row's registry only, with the row's final repository (no renormalization).** **Plane:** DEVDESK-304, dated 2026-11-13. Sources: `.claude/plans/DEVDESK-304-plan.md`, `docs/product/image-search/stories.md`, D129, D130, D131, `docs/architecture/network.md` ("`→` at level 1").
131:5. **Open point (handled by D133).** An `esc` from tags opened by `→` does not cancel the lot, so a late failure can show `Could not load tags` over the form. Handled by DEVDESK-307 (IS-09): leaving the tags cancels the lot.
135:**D131 — DEVDESK-301 (IS-02): the Docker Hub searcher is active in production as soon as it lands, not behind a flag; a registry that is not Hub answers `imagesearch.ErrUnsupported` with no request and is logged at INFO, with nothing visible; Hub names are validated by a regex, validated per OCI component (`^[a-z0-9]+(?:(?:[._]|__|-+)[a-z0-9]+)*$`, accepts `e__f` and `a--b`). Decided (activation chosen by the user).** **Plane:** DEVDESK-301 (IS-02), dated 2026-11-13. Sources: `.claude/plans/DEVDESK-301-302-297-plan.md`, `docs/product/image-search/stories.md` (IS-02), D129, `docs/architecture/network.md` ("Image search"). `defaultImageSearcher` is `ByRegistry(HubSearcher{}, nil)`, so level 1 and Open Tags are on; D129's "inactive until IS-02" ends here. Until IS-03 every private registry gets `ErrUnsupported`, which is not shown (a visible error would greet every non-Hub user). Hub's name rules follow the OCI spec regex per component (`^[a-z0-9]+(?:(?:[._]|__|-+)[a-z0-9]+)*$`); the first draft rejected `e__f`, which no longer applies. Descriptions also lose Unicode Cf characters, and the typed text goes to Docker Hub once a Hub entry is checked. Local, reversible decision: no ADR.
137:**D130 — DEVDESK-300 (IS-11; point 1 superseded by D131): « Open tags » is a second button of the registry browser's form, beside « Search », shown only once a `Searcher` is wired; one button « Browse Tags » until then. `enter` in the header follows the focus, and is lit on Repository (correcting Rule 130). Decided (Q1 to Q4, chosen by the user on 2026-11-12).** **Plane:** DEVDESK-300 (IS-11), dated 2026-11-12. Sources: `.claude/plans/DEVDESK-300-plan.md` (branch `feat/devdesk-300-open-tags`, untracked when this entry was written), `docs/product/image-search/` (IS-11, IS-01), D129, Rule 130 in `.claude/rules/tui-layout.md`, Rules 135 and 137 in `.claude/rules/tui-forms.md` and `tui-layout.md`.
139:1. **One button until a `Searcher` exists (Q1, option A; superseded by D131).** While `defaultImageSearcher` is `nil` (production until IS-02), the form keeps today's single button, « Browse Tags », which lists the tags of the typed name. With a `Searcher`, the form shows « Search » and « Open Tags » on one line. Rejected: B (two buttons that do the same thing in production) and C (a greyed « Search » with a warning, a dead button visible until IS-02). Consequence: IS-11 is proved by tests with an injected fake `Searcher`, not by hand before IS-02.
143:5. **Behaviour shared by both actions.** Open tags reuses `startTagLookup` unchanged: no new request, same credentials, generation and cancellation (IS-18); the registry selection applies to both actions; a short name is not routed to level 1 by Open tags.
147:**D129 — DEVDESK-298, DEVDESK-299, DEVDESK-397 (point 1 superseded by D131): the image search's level 1 ships inactive in production until IS-02 lands; `esc` at level 1 cancels the lot; request generations are one global counter; `StatusError` keeps its messages through an unexported field. Decided.** **Plane:** DEVDESK-298 (IS-18), DEVDESK-299 (IS-01), dated 2026-11-12. Sources: `.claude/plans/DEVDESK-299-plan.md` (untracked), `docs/product/image-search/`, PR #383 (DEVDESK-298), branch `feat-devdesk-299-image-search-level1` (uncommitted when this entry was written).
149:1. **Level 1 is inactive in production (superseded by D131).** `defaultImageSearcher` is `nil`, and the browser routes a name with no `/` to level 1 only when it has a `Searcher` (option A of Q1). Otherwise `nginx` would give an empty table and the direct path to the tags of `nginx` would disappear until IS-02 (the Hub adapter) and IS-11 ("Open tags") ship. Rejected: B (active now, a searcher that finds nothing: a visible regression) and C (a long-lived branch, conflicts with IS-15). Consequence: the criteria of IS-01 are proved by tests with an injected fake, not by hand; the only visible change is the "No registry selected" warning. IS-02 sets `defaultImageSearcher`.
153:5. **Known limit.** The HTTP client's 15 s `Timeout` per request also wraps `context.DeadlineExceeded`, so IS-12 cannot tell it from the 15 s per-registry deadline (`imageSearchDeadline`); both read as a failed registry. A search error is only logged (`jobs.SafeCause`) until IS-12.

  ## Plan en 7 étapes, chacune testable en TDD
  
  1. **`Classify` pour un résultat partiel sans ligne** (`internal/imagesearch/verdict.go`) : dépend de Q1.
  2. **Durcir `isDHI`** (D134 point 9) : passer par `url.Parse` et `Hostname()`, pour couvrir les identifiants dans l'URL, l'IPv6, le port et le point final.
  3. **`oci.ListCatalogContext`** (nouveau `internal/oci/catalog.go`) :
     - parcours de `/v2/_catalog?n=1000` en suivant l'en-tête `Link`, au plus 10 pages et 1 MiB par page ;
     - un lien `next` vers une autre origine n'est pas suivi, pour ne pas envoyer les identifiants à un hôte tiers ;
     - l'authentification Basic puis Bearer et le jeton gardé d'une page à l'autre reprennent le flux des tags, qui ne change pas.
  4. **Fonctions de noms communes** (`imagesearch/names.go`) : `validRepoPath` (l'ancienne regex `hubComponent`) et `MatchTier`, déplacé depuis l'UI. C'est un refactor pur ; les tests existants restent verts sans modification.
  5. **`imagesearch.CatalogSearcher`** (nouveau `catalog.go`), avec un `List` injectable :
     - une saisie de moins de 2 caractères donne `ErrQueryTooShort`, sans aucune requête ;
     - la garde R1 s'applique avant le filtre, et seulement si le parcours est complet ;
     - le filtre porte sur la partie du nom après le préfixe ;
     - les correspondances sont triées par `MatchTier`, puis coupées à 100 lignes, ce qui donne `partial`.
  
     Les tests `httptest` sur `_catalog` reportés par D134 point 7 sont ici, un par critère de 1 à 8.

  - **Q1 (bloquante, D134 H1 demande de la trancher ici)** : quel verdict pour un parcours coupé au plafond sans aucune correspondance, ou sans aucun nom portant le préfixe ? Aujourd'hui, `Classify(nil, 0, true)` rend « no result » sans marque.
    - **A (recommandée)** : « no result » avec la marque `Partial`. Cela change l'invariant « `Partial` seulement avec ok », et IS-13 devra l'afficher.
    - **B** : on garde le comportement actuel. Un « no result » peut alors être faux sans que rien ne le signale.
    - **C** : « refused ». C'est faux, puisque le registre a répondu.
  
    Seules l'étape 1 et deux cas de test de l'étape 5 en dépendent.
  - **Q2 (non bloquante)** : `→` pendant une recherche annule le lot (D132 point 4, « à revoir avant IS-03 »). Avec les catalogues, les recherches seront plus lentes, donc cela arrivera plus souvent. Par défaut je ne change rien dans IS-03 ; s'il faut changer, ce sera une story séparée.
  - **Q3 (non bloquante)** : pour une entrée avec préfixe, la colonne Name affiche-t-elle `api` ou `docker-hosted/api` ? Par défaut : `api`. La référence, elle, reste `docker-hosted/api` (critère 2).
  
  ## Hypothèses à signaler dans la PR (H1 à H6 dans le plan)
  
  - Le seuil « 1 caractère » se compte en runes, après suppression des espaces autour.
  - Une page en erreur au milieu du parcours rend le registre « failed », sans ligne gardée.
  - Un lien `next` vers une autre origine rend le parcours partiel, sans erreur.
  - `Query.Limit` peut seulement réduire le plafond de 100 lignes.
  - La ligne de journal R1 contient le préfixe : il n'est pas secret et aide à diagnostiquer Nexus.
  
  ## Risques
  
  - **R1 sur Nexus** : invérifiable sans un vrai Nexus (IS-16 est bloquée).
  - **Plusieurs entrées sur un même hôte** : chacune refait le parcours complet du catalogue (c'est IS-07, hors MVP).
  - **`_catalog` n'est pas dans la spec OCI** : un registre qui ne l'expose pas répond 404, ce qui donne « refused » ; c'est le comportement voulu.
  - **Identifiants envoyés au realm Bearer** : ils partent vers le realm annoncé par le registre. C'est déjà le cas pour les tags aujourd'hui, et je ne le change pas.
  
  Rien n'est irréversible : aucune donnée ni configuration persistée ne change. Je ne propose pas d'ADR.
</agent-message>

content.text:
Base directory for this skill: /home/anthoni/projects/workspace-entire/anthnel/devdesk/.claude/skills/git-worktree-pr

## Work starts in a new worktree

**Any task that will produce a commit begins with its own worktree**, cut from
the current `main`, **under `.worktrees/` inside the repository**:

```bash
git fetch origin main
git worktree add -b <branch> .worktrees/<branch> origin/main
cd .worktrees/<branch>
```

Answering a question, reading code, running the app — none of that needs one.
Editing does.

**Under the repository, not beside it.** This reverses what this file said until
now, and the reason it gave was wrong. It claimed a worktree at `.worktrees/x`
would be compiled by `go build ./...` and `go test ./...`. It would not: the go
tool skips every directory whose name begins with `.` or `_`, so `.worktrees/`
is invisible to `./...`. Verified rather than assumed — a package of deliberately
invalid Go placed under `.worktrees/` builds clean and `go list ./...` does not
name it. The old argument holds for `worktrees/` without the dot, which is
presumably where it came from.

What decides it is the **sandbox mount**, and it cost a full debugging session to
find. A direct-mode sandbox mounts *this directory only*. A sibling worktree at
`../devdesk-<branch>` is therefore outside the mount, so its **files** are written
into the container's private layer and never reach the host — while `.git` is
inside the mount and stays shared. Refs agree, files diverge, and nothing warns:
the branch tip moves, the host's copy of those files does not, and `git status`
on the host reports the *stale* content as uncommitted modifications. An agent
and the person testing its work end up compiling different code while both
believe they are on the same branch. Under `.worktrees/`, host and sandbox see
one filesystem.

  - `https://example.com/dhi.io`

- `REDACTED`
- `ftp://dhi.io`

Exactement `maxPages*pageSize` noms sans `next` donne `truncated=false`. Une boucle de `next` est bornée par `resolveNext` et par `maxPages`.

Rien de nouveau sur ce point.
  - **Jeton entre les pages** : réutilisé seulement sur la même origine, grâce à la garde ci-dessus (sous la réserve des redirections du premier constat).

  - registry.go:108 : le flux des tags suit un `next` vers n'importe quel hôte avec Basic ou Bearer. C'est plus grave que la redirection, car Go ne retire pas l'en-tête puisque c'est une nouvelle requête construite par le code. À traiter dans un ticket séparé en réutilisant `sameOrigin`.
